question: Between 3 and 6 November, more than 20 commercial aircraft operating intra-EU flights were targeted by bomb alerts, suggesting coordinated action. Investigations are ongoing, but several airport authorities have referred to alerts attributed to Russian extremist and masculinist groups.

More broadly, these threats to European aviation security arise in the context of an increase in hybrid attacks targeting the EU, with 50 000 Global Navigation Satellite System jamming and spoofing incidents recorded in Europe in 2025 alone. In view of the above, does the Commission envisage: 1.
Proposing sanctions against the entities identified as responsible once the investigations are completed?
Conducting a stress test of Europe’s air traffic management capabilities to assess their ability to handle a large number of such alerts simultaneously?

Adopting measures to assess and strengthen the cyber resilience of EU airports and other strategic dual-use infrastructure, notably by banning components from high-risk suppliers, for example within the framework of the implementing act referred to in Article 34 of the proposal for a regulation on military mobility1?

Proposal of 19 November 2025 for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on establishing a framework of measures to facilitate the transport of military equipment, goods and personnel across the Union, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025PC0847. 1
